s: Which one of the following guilds was primarily associated with domestic trade during the Kakatiya period?
x: Nakaram was the guild associated with domestic trade. Nanadesi Pekkandru specialised in foreign trade, while Ubhaya Nanadesi operated in both markets.
tq: Use the scope of each guild to distinguish closely related trade organisations.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: The Nanadesi Pekkandru guild was mainly connected with
x: Nanadesi Pekkandru was a foreign-trade guild. Nakaram was associated with domestic trade, whereas Ubhaya Nanadesi dealt in both domestic and foreign markets.
tq: Test the exact meaning of a similar-sounding guild name.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Nakaram — Domestic trade
2. Nanadesi Pekkandru — Foreign trade
3. Ubhaya Nanadesi Pekkandru — Domestic and foreign trade
4. Ayyavali Ainuraru — Guild of 500

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Nakaram handled domestic trade, Nanadesi foreign trade, Ubhaya Nanadesi both types of trade, and Ayyavali Ainuraru was the guild of 500.
tq: Check every pair against the guild’s specialised scope or numerical identity.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Virabanajam was licensed to operate in which of the following regions?
x: The Virabanajam guild was licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda, as recorded in the Tripurantakam inscription of 1282.
tq: Recall the specific licensed regions rather than confusing them with ports or foreign trading partners.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: The Tripurantakam inscription of 1282 is associated with the licensing of
o: Virabanajam in Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda
x: The Tripurantakam inscription of 1282 records the areas in which Virabanajam was licensed to operate: Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda.
tq: Link the inscription, date and guild through the distinctive licensing detail.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Ayyavali Ainuraru is best described as
o: An official body collecting port duties
A guild restricted to domestic trade
x: Ayyavali Ainuraru was the great trans-regional merchant guild known as the guild of 500.
tq: Use the numerical identity in the guild’s name to identify the organisation.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was NOT a function or characteristic of the Kakatiya merchant guilds?
o: Exercising an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade
Maintaining their own seal or emblem
x: Guilds maintained seals or emblems, settled disputes and kept private military forces, but they did not possess an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade.
tq: Find the overbroad and exclusive statement that goes beyond the guild functions.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding merchant guilds:

1. A merchant was called a Behari.
2. Trade was referred to as Vyavaharam.
3. The head of a guild was called Setti or Sreshthi.
4. Guild members were drawn exclusively from Vaishyas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Guild members came from several communities, including Settis, Reddis, Nayakulu, Boyas, Dasaris and Vaishyas, so statement 4 is false.
tq: Reject the exclusive-membership statement and retain the precise occupational terms.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the economic and administrative functions of merchant guilds?
o: Temple priests, military commanders and village headmen
Bankers, local administrators and negotiators for tax concessions
Coin minters, irrigation engineers and royal ambassadors
Judges, royal tax collectors and hereditary governors only
x: Merchant guilds acted as bankers and local administrators and negotiated with the king for tax concessions. The Motupalli charter illustrates this interaction.
tq: Identify the option that combines the guild’s economic, administrative and negotiating roles.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was included among the exports of the Kakatiya period?
o: Iron tools, salt and timber only
Perfumes, horses, porcelain and silk alone
Grain, copper and medicinal herbs alone
x: The listed exports were textiles, spices, diamonds and gold. Perfumes and spices were mentioned among the imports.
tq: Distinguish the export list from the shorter list of imports.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was mentioned as an import in Kakatiya overseas trade?
x: Perfumes were among the imports. Textiles, diamonds and gold were listed among the exports.
tq: Use the export-import reversal trap with commodities appearing in both trade contexts.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s:
The Kakatiya trade network had commercial links with which of the following regions or countries?

1. China
2. Persia
3. Arabia
4. Ceylon
5. East Indies

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The recorded trading partners included China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon and the East Indies.
tq: Verify the complete list instead of stopping after identifying the first few familiar partners.
sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

s: Ports collecting import and export duties were known as
x: Ports that collected import and export duties were called Kara Pattanam.
tq: Distinguish the technical term for duty-collecting ports from names of actual ports and guilds.

s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam was issued by Ganapatideva in
x: Ganapatideva issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244 CE at Motupalli.
tq: Place the inscription date among the nearby dates associated with other inscriptions and periods.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam:

1. It guaranteed safety to foreign merchants.
2. It remitted arbitrary taxes.
3. It promised compensation for losses caused by shipwreck or theft.
4. It authorised harassment of merchants by local officials.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The charter protected foreign merchants, remitted arbitrary taxes and promised compensation for losses from shipwreck or theft. It stopped, rather than authorised, harassment by officials.
tq: Identify the reversed negative statement concerning official harassment.

s: Who was appointed at Motupalli under the Abhaya Sasanam of Ganapatideva?
x: Siddayya Devudu was the official posted at Motupalli under Ganapatideva’s charter.
tq: Match the official with the charter and port, avoiding confusion with later rulers and builders.

s: In the expression ‘Abhaya Sasanam’, the word ‘Abhaya’ conveys the idea of
x: ‘Abhaya’ means assurance of safety. The charter used this principle to protect foreign and seafaring traders.
tq: Use the literal meaning of the key term to identify the charter’s purpose.

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Arikesari Samudram — Prola II
2. Ramappa tank — Recherla Rudra
3. Pakhala tank — Mummadi Nayaka
4. Laknavaram — Ganapatideva
x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Arikesari Samudram was built by Prola II, Ramappa tank by Recherla Rudra, Pakhala tank by Mummadi Nayaka, and Laknavaram by Ganapatideva.
tq: Start with the sure builder-tank pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped ruler or tank.

s: Who constructed the Ghanapuram tank?
x: Ghanapuram tank was constructed by Ganapatideva.
tq: Test a direct builder-tank association from the irrigation record.

s: Bayyaram tank is associated with which builder?
o: Surambika, wife of Peda Komati Vema
Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka
x: Bayyaram tank was built by Mailamba, the sister of Ganapati.
tq: Use the kinship detail to distinguish the builder from other tank patrons.

s: Kunda Samudram, also called Chouda Samudram, was associated with
x: Kunda Samudram or Chouda Samudram was associated with Kundamamba and Malyala Chauda respectively.
tq: Combine alternative names with their associated patrons to avoid splitting one tank into two unrelated entries.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Pakhala tank was built by Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka, not by Mailamba. Mailamba was associated with Bayyaram tank.
tq: Find the swapped builder by comparing patrons of neighbouring tanks.

s:
Which one of the following statements about tank irrigation is correct?

1. Large tanks were called Samudrams.
2. Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks.
3. Surplus water could pass downhill from one tank to the next.
4. Dashabandhamu referred to tax-free land assigned for tank maintenance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four statements are correct. Samudrams were large tanks, Golusukattu cheruvulu formed linked chains, surplus flowed to lower tanks, and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for upkeep.
tq: Confirm the complete irrigation-system description, including the maintenance arrangement.

s: Tank-building was counted among the Sapta Santanalu, which refers to
x: Sapta Santanalu means seven meritorious works. The list included a son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.
tq: Distinguish a cultural-religious classification from administrative and fiscal categories.

s: Which of the following was NOT included among the Sapta Santanalu?
x: The Sapta Santanalu included son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure. A merchant guild was not one of the seven meritorious works.
tq: Eliminate the item belonging to trade rather than the list of meritorious works.

s: The Porumamilla tank inscription is associated with which combination?
o: 1369, Bhaskara, son of Bukka I, Vijayanagara period
1416, Deva Raya I, Motupalli, Reddi period
x: The Porumamilla tank inscription dates to 1369 and was issued by Bhaskara, son of Vijayanagara ruler Bukka I. It belongs to the Vijayanagara period and lists twelve requisites of a good tank.
tq: Combine date, person, dynasty and inscription subject to separate similar records.

s: The Porumamilla inscription is particularly important in the study of irrigation because it
o: records the twelve requisites of a good tank
defines the five classes of merchant guilds
records the tax rates on imported perfumes
lists the foreign merchants protected at Motupalli
x: The Porumamilla inscription of 1369 lists twelve requisites of a good tank. It is from the Vijayanagara period, though it is often studied alongside Kakatiya irrigation works.
tq: Identify the inscription from its distinctive technical subject rather than its dynasty alone.

s: Which one of the following places was noted for the production of iron during the Kakatiya period?
x: Guthikonda and Palnadu were known for iron production. Nirmal was associated with knives, while Warangal was known for carpets and textiles.
tq: Use the industry–centre association and eliminate nearby but different craft centres.

s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Ratna kambalu — Warangal
2. Knives — Nirmal
3. Diamonds — Golconda region
4. Iron — Warangal

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Ratna kambalu was associated with Warangal, knives with Nirmal and diamonds with the Golconda region. Iron was associated with Guthikonda and Palnadu, not Warangal.
tq: Start from the sure industry–centre pairs and identify the reversed association.

s: Marco Polo is said to have remarked that the fineness of which Kakatiya textile was such that a seven-yard saree could fit into a matchbox?
x: Marco Polo is said to have described the extremely fine cloth of the region in this manner; the material is identified as fine muslin.
tq: Test the distinctive traveller–observation association directly.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding painting in Orugallu during the Kakatiya period?
o: Machaladevi was a male court painter of the Kalyani Chalukyas.
Painting was confined to the Golconda region and had no association with Orugallu.
Orugallu had about 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi was a woman painter.
Orugallu had about 150 painters' houses, led by Machaladevi.
x: Orugallu is described as having 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi is identified as a woman painter.
tq: Separate the precise number from the nearby wrong figure and swapped identity.

s:
Which of the following statements about Kakatiya economic activity is correct?

1. Cotton growing and weaving were major activities.
2. Fine muslin was exported.
3. Diamond trade was associated with the Golconda region.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Cotton cultivation and weaving were major activities, fine muslin was exported, and the Golconda region was associated with diamond trade.
tq: Check each economic activity independently before choosing the combined code.

s: The Nayankara system in its reorganised Kakatiya form is principally associated with which ruler?
x: Prataparudra II is identified with the introduction or reorganisation of the Nayankara system in the Kakatiya kingdom.
tq: Use the ruler–administrative reform association without confusing earlier Kakatiya rulers.

s: Which one of the following best describes the Nayankara system?
o: Military commanders were made administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and were assigned responsibility for forts.
Temple authorities collected all taxes and maintained the royal army.
Civil scribes were appointed as village accountants without military duties.
Merchants were granted exclusive control over provincial administration.
x: Under the Nayankara system, military commanders served as administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and protected specified forts.
tq: Identify the institutional arrangement from the roles performed by the Nayakas.

s: Which of the following was NOT an obligation of a Kakatiya Nayaka holding Nayakasthalam?
o: Paying a fixed annual sum or tribute to the king
Keeping the entire revenue without any payment to the king
Maintaining a fixed military force for the king
Remitting the remaining revenue after meeting prescribed obligations
x: A Nayaka retained a share of revenue for maintaining troops, paid a fixed annual sum to the king and remitted the balance. The entire revenue was not retained.
tq: Find the option that reverses the stated revenue and military obligations.

s: The villages assigned to Nayakas in lieu of salary were known as:
x: Nayakas received villages called Nayakasthalam instead of a regular salary, drawing revenue from them to meet their obligations.
tq: Discriminate between the Kakatiya grant term and the later Vijayanagara term Amaram.

s: The Kakatiya Nayankara system was continued in a modified form by the Vijayanagara rulers as the:
x: Vijayanagara continued the arrangement as the Amara-Nayankara system. The land was called Amaram and the tribute was known as Kappam or Kist.
tq: Match the earlier administrative institution with its later institutional form.

s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with the Vijayanagara continuation of the Nayankara system?
o: Amaram — land; Kappam or Kist — tribute
Amaram — village accountant; Kappam — grazing tax
Amaram — judicial office; Kist — marriage tax
x: In the Vijayanagara form, the land assignment was called Amaram and the tribute was called Kappam or Kist.
tq: Separate the names of the land assignment and tribute from unrelated administrative terms.

s: The break-up of the Amara-Nayankara system is associated with the emergence of the:
x: The break-up of the Amara-Nayankara system produced the Poligars.
tq: Test the institutional legacy through its historical consequence.

s:
Which of the following works are cited as sources for the study of the Nayankara system?

1. Baddena's Neeti Sastra Muktavali
2. Ekamranatha's Pratapa Charitra
3. Shivadevayya's Purushartha Saram

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Baddena's Neeti Sastra Muktavali and Ekamranatha's Pratapa Charitra are cited as sources for the Nayankara system. Purushartha Saram is associated with information on the 72 Niyogas.
tq: Distinguish sources for the Nayankara system from a source for central departments.

s:
Arrange the following administrative units from the largest to the smallest:

A. Grama
B. Rashtra or Mandala
C. Sthala
D. Nadu or Bhumi

Select the correct sequence.
x: Rashtra or Mandala was the largest province, followed by Nadu or Bhumi, Sthala and finally Grama.
tq: Arrange administrative units by territorial scale, using the largest and smallest as anchors.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Sthala — a group of about 20 villages
Grama — largest province under a prince
x: A Sthala consisted of about 20 villages. Rashtra was the largest province, while Grama denoted a village.
tq: Use the hierarchy of territorial units to reject swapped meanings.

s: In Kakatiya administration, the term 'Karanam' denoted the:
o: Village headman responsible for revenue and order
x: Karanam was the village accountant. The Reddi was the village headman, Talari the village watchman and Sunkadhikari the toll collector.
tq: Discriminate among closely related village and revenue offices.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pradvivaka — collector of customs and tolls
x: Pradvivaka was an adviser to the king on the judicial system. The Sunkadhikari or Sunkamanya collected customs and tolls.
tq: Find the swapped official function in a list of administrative offices.

s: The 72 central departments under the Kakatiyas were known as Niyogas and were placed under the:
x: The central departments were called 72 Niyogas and were supervised by the Bahattara Niyogadhipati.
tq: Link the distinctive number with the corresponding supervising authority.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the council comprising Pradhani, Pragada, Amatya, Mantri and Senadhipati?
x: Sunkamanya was a collector of tolls and customs. The other three named officials, along with Pragada and Mantri, formed the stated council.
tq: Use exclusion from the stated council rather than confusing a revenue officer with a ministerial office.

s: Who served as prime minister during the reign of Ganapatideva according to the administrative record?
x: Malyala Hemadri Reddi served as prime minister under Ganapatideva. Muppidi Nayudu served under Prataparudra.
tq: Test the ruler–prime minister association and avoid swapping the two reigns.

s: Which description of the nature of the Kakatiya state is correctly matched with the scholar?
x: Most scholars describe the Kakatiya state as a decentralised monarchy. Romila Thapar called it a metropolitan state, while Burton Stein compared it to a segmentary state.
tq: Keep the three scholarly characterisations separate instead of treating them as synonyms.

s: Land revenue during the Kakatiya period was generally fixed at what fraction of the produce?
x: Land revenue, referred to as bhaga or Ari, was generally one-sixth of the produce.
tq: Identify the precise revenue fraction and reject nearby traditional shares.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Magani from Metta?
o: Magani was irrigated wet land, whereas Metta was rain-fed dry land.
Magani was rain-fed dry land, whereas Metta was irrigated wet land.
Both terms denoted newly cultivated forest land.
x: Magani denoted irrigated wet land, generally used for food crops, while Metta denoted rain-fed dry land.
tq: Test the reversed meaning of two similar land-classification terms.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiya taxes is correct?

1. Sunkam meant customs or tolls.
2. Angadisunkam was a tax on weekly markets.
3. Pullari was a grazing tax.
4. Pellipannu was a marriage tax.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four statements are correct: Sunkam was customs or tolls, Angadisunkam a weekly-market tax, Pullari a grazing tax and Pellipannu a marriage tax.
tq: Verify each tax against its taxable activity before selecting the complete combination.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its land category?
x: Thotapolam denoted garden land. Podu was newly cultivated land, Velipolam was rain-fed dry land and Magani was irrigated wet land.
tq: Identify the exact land-category meaning and reject reversed classifications.

s: Which one of the following statements about land rights and taxation is correct?
o: All forest land was permanently exempt from taxation.
Temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands paid the highest land revenue.
Dashabandhamu referred to lands maintained for tanks.
x: Dashabandhamu referred to lands connected with tank maintenance. Arigapulu were tax-paying farmers, while temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands were tax-exempt.
tq: Match the land category with its fiscal treatment and reject absolute claims.

s: Forest land was cleared with tax concessions primarily to:
o: Transfer all forest revenue to temples
x: Tax concessions on cleared forest land were intended to encourage settlement and cultivation.
tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the stated fiscal concession.

s: The twelve village functionaries known as Ayagars were generally remunerated through:
o: Only gold coins issued by the king
A fixed share of customs collected at ports
Shares of produce and service lands
x: The twelve Ayagars were paid through shares of produce and service lands.
tq: Distinguish the village-service remuneration system from military land assignments.
sec: Society → ayagars, caste mobility, women donors

s: Which one of the following pairs of women donors and tanks is correctly matched?
o: Mailamba — Bayyaram tank; Kundamamba — Kunda Samudram
Mailamba — Kunda Samudram; Kundamamba — Bayyaram tank
Mailamba — Warangal fort; Kundamamba — Bayyaram tank
x: Mailamba is associated with the Bayyaram tank and Kundamamba with Kunda Samudram.
tq: Start with the sure donor–tank pair and avoid swapping the two women.
sec: Society → ayagars, caste mobility, women donors

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the number and territorial control of Nayankaras is correct?

1. There were 72 Nayankaras, according to one account.
2. Each Nayankara guarded a fort.
3. Nayankaras controlled one-fourth of the kingdom's land.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: One account gives the number as 72; each Nayankara guarded a fort, and the Nayankaras controlled one-fourth of the kingdom's land.
tq: Combine the numerical, military and territorial facts without confusing them with the 75 or 77 principalities account.
sec: Number of Nayakas and fort bastions under Prataparudra

s: Which of the following groups consisted of the three generals of Prataparudra who survived the events of 1323?
o: Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama and Prolaya Vemareddy
Racherla Rudra, Natavadi Buddharaja and Kundamamba
Malyala Hemadri Reddi, Muppidi Nayudu and Prolaya Nayaka
x: The three surviving generals named are Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama and Prolaya Vemareddy.
tq: Use the complete name-set to distinguish the surviving generals from rulers and officials.
sec: Number of Nayakas and fort bastions under Prataparudra

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Ari denoted land revenue or Bhumi sistu. Koru was levied on wet land, Pullari was a grazing tax, and Kanika was a customary gift.
tq: Start from the sure meaning and eliminate the swapped tax descriptions.

s: The tax levied on wet or Magani land during the Kakatiya period was known as
x: Koru was the tax imposed on wet or Magani land. Putti Pahindi was the tax on dry land.
tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between wet-land and dry-land taxes.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putti Pahindi — Tax on dry land
x: Pellipannu was a wedding tax, not a cattle tax. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
tq: Find the one wrong description among closely related taxes and cesses.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pullari — Grazing or grass-land tax
2. Kanika — Customary gift to the king or officials
3. Alam — Tax on vegetables or produce
4. Angadi Sunkam — Wedding tax
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Pullari, Kanika and Alam are correctly matched. Angadi Sunkam was a weekly-market tax, whereas Pellipannu was the wedding tax.
tq: Split the options by checking the easily confused market and wedding cesses.

s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the other agricultural levies of the Kakatiya period?
x: Siddhayam, Ardhayam and Niruvidi were agricultural levies. Dari Sunkam was a road toll and belonged to the category of other sunkams.
tq: Classify each term by its levy category before selecting the exception.

s: Which of the following was included among the other sunkams mentioned in the Kakatiya period?
x: Burra, Madiga, Gandi and Revu were named as other sunkams. Koru, Pellipannu and Putti Pahindi had specific descriptions as land or social taxes.
tq: Direct recall from a named list, with nearby tax terms as distractors.

s: The village functionaries collectively known as Ayagars were primarily associated with which combination of activities?
x: The Ayagars handled village revenue, order, irrigation and records. Their functions were administrative and local rather than confined to temples or foreign trade.
tq: Identify the administrative cluster that fits the village-functionary system.
sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the usual list of Kakatiya Ayagars?
x: Karanam was included among the Ayagars and was associated with village records. Gaja Sahini, Padmanayaka and Chaturanga belonged to military terminology.
tq: Separate village offices from military designations before matching.
sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of names included in the usual list of Ayagars?
o: Gaja Sahini, Ashwa Sahini, Mula Balam, Padmanayaka
x: Karanam, Reddi, Talari and Purohita were all village functionaries in the Ayagar system. The other groups contain military, trade-centre or taxation terms.
tq: Check whether all items belong to the same institutional list.
sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

s: The usual mode of payment to an Ayagar consisted of
o: Cash salary alone from the royal treasury
Military jagirs without any agricultural share
Tax-free manyam land and a share of each harvest
A share in customs duties collected at ports
x: Ayagars received tax-free Ayagar or manyam land together with a share of each harvest instead of cash payment.
tq: Discriminate between land-and-harvest payment and cash or military remuneration.
sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

s: Chaturanga bala in the Kakatiya military organisation referred to
x: Chaturanga bala means the army organised into four arms. It is a military classification, not a classification of forts, officers or taxes.
tq: Use the literal institutional context to distinguish the military term.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s: The army of Prataparudra is stated to have consisted of approximately
x: The figures associated with Prataparudra's army were 100 elephants, 20,000 cavalry and 900,000 infantry.
tq: Keep the three arms and their figures together instead of matching numbers independently.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiya military divisions is correct?
1. Mula Balam was the king's standing army.
2. The Nayankara army formed the other major division.
3. Mula Balam consisted exclusively of village functionaries.
x: Mula Balam was the king's standing army, and the Nayankara army was the other major division. The third statement is false because Mula Balam was a military division, not a body of village functionaries.
tq: Reject the extreme exclusive description after identifying the two genuine divisions.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gaja Sahini — Jayapa Senani under Ganapatideva
Ashwa Sahini — Jayapa Senani under Ganapatideva
Gaja Sahini — Maraya under Prataparudra II
Ashwa Sahini — Induluri Annayya under Prataparudra II
x: Jayapa Senani held the position of Gaja Sahini under Ganapatideva. Gangaya Sahini was associated with Ashwa Sahini under Ganapatideva, while Maraya held that position under Prataparudra II.
tq: Match the corps head with both the correct corps and ruler.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s: Padmanayakas in the Kakatiya period were
o: A group of port merchants from Motupalli
Village accountants paid only in cash
Recherla Velama chiefs and important Kakatiya commanders
x: Padmanayakas were Recherla Velama chiefs and key Kakatiya commanders. They later founded the Velama kingdom.
tq: Use the person-group and later political role to identify the correct description.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
x: Giridurga means a hill fort. Jaladurga was a water fort, Vanadurga a forest fort and Sthaladurga a plain fort.
tq: Discriminate among similar fort names by their environmental prefixes.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s: Which statement about the Warangal fort is correct?
o: It was a water fort without any surrounding land defence.
It was exclusively a forest fort without defensive walls.
It consisted only of a single wall on a hill.
It had concentric walls and a moat.
x: Warangal fort was characterised by concentric walls and a moat. Its defensive design was not limited to a single wall or a purely natural setting.
tq: Select the precise structural feature rather than the generic fort type.
sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

s: Which one of the following ports was located on the Nellore coast?
x: Krishnapatnam was situated on the Nellore coast. Hamsaladeevi was associated with the Krishna delta, while Machilipatnam was associated with Krishna.
